status: Source regression fixed; packaged fault check pending
cause: An unexpected scene removal reached terrain._exit_tree and backend.stop after sibling state owners had left the tree. stop captured addon state again, allowing detached zombie/corpse transforms or other teardown-time state to replace the previous compound checkpoint.
correction: For gameplay worlds requiring published shutdown, _exit_tree disables new snapshot writes unless graceful shutdown already stopped the terrain. Explicit attached-world shutdown remains unchanged. No readiness, scheduling, mining or native storage format change.
scope: Direct scene teardown is not a substitute for Save and Quit. It preserves the verified checkpoint instead of attempting a late snapshot from unavailable providers.

before.evidence: Real native terrain/archive and inventory provider; direct scene removal invoked a detached sibling capture, changed canonical file bytes and restored unsaved teardown state in a fresh worker. A later expectation then failed because it inherited that wrong state.

after.evidence: Direct removal makes no detached capture and preserves exact canonical hash; fresh worker restores old inventory. Attached graceful shutdown still persists new inventory and does not recapture on removal.

Existing shutdown ordering regression: excavation publication, inventory reward ordering, fresh reload, rejected edit during close, failed publication and invalid addon capture retain canonical checkpoint.
